title: Realizing a single derived invertible action by equivariant complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], $P:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ an additive exact autoequivalence, $\mathcal B=\mathcal A^P$ the fixed-pair category [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], and $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ its forgetful functor. Use ordinary derived categories and their cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $M\in D(\mathcal B)$ write $\theta_M:D(P)D(U)M\xrightarrow{\sim}D(U)M$ for the isomorphism induced by the structure maps of a representing complex.

For every $N\in D(\mathcal A)$ with bounded cohomology and every isomorphism $v:D(P)N\xrightarrow{\sim}N$, there exist $M\in D(\mathcal B)$ and an isomorphism $e:D(U)M\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ such that
$$e\theta_M=vD(P)(e).$$
The cohomology of $M$ is bounded in the same interval as that of $N$. If $\mathcal S$ is any isomorphism-invariant class of objects of $\mathcal A$ and every $H^i(N)$ lies in $\mathcal S$, then every underlying cohomology object $U H^i(M)$ lies in $\mathcal S$. No functorial choice of $M$ or equivalence of derived categories with fixed-pair categories is asserted.

proof.text: Choose a complex representing N and a K-injective resolution I, using lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective. Let a:QI≅N. Exact derivation identifies Q(PI) with D(P)(QI). By lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived, lift the morphism Q(PI)→D(P)(QI)→D(P)N→N→QI to a chain map f:PI→I. Its image under Q is invertible, so f is a quasi-isomorphism by def-weil-abstract-derived-category. Exact faithful forgetting for fixed pairs is already supplied by the adopted IsoAlgebra source library; no right-derived-forgetting comparison is used.

proof.text: Choose a quasi-inverse $R$ of $P$ with unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}RP$ and counit $\epsilon:PR\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ satisfying the triangle identities. Put $g=R(f)\eta_I:I\to RI$, $X_n=R^nI$ and $g_n=R^n(g):X_n\to X_{n+1}$ for $n\geq0$. These are actual complexes and chain maps. An equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels by [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits], hence $R$ is exact. Consequently all $g_n$ are quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Let $C=\operatorname{colim}_{n\in\mathbf N}X_n$ degreewise, with legs $j_n$. These colimits exist by [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. The equations $d_{X_{n+1}}g_n=g_nd_{X_n}$ give a differential on $C$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; its square is zero since it is zero after every $j_n$. The indexing category is the nonempty directed poset $\mathbf N$, so its colimits are filtered.

proof.text: Filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$ are exact by [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Applying [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] gives $H^q(C)\cong\operatorname{colim}_nH^q(X_n)$, with cocone legs $H^q(j_n)$. Every transition is an isomorphism. To check the initial leg is invertible, let $h_n:H^q(I)\to H^q(X_n)$ be the composite of the first $n$ transition maps, with $h_0=1$. The inverses $h_n^{-1}$ form a cocone and induce an inverse to the initial leg: one composite is the identity at $n=0$, and the other is the identity after each colimit leg since $h_{n+1}=H^q(g_n)h_n$. The colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] proves both equalities. Thus $j_0:I\to C$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: For the chain-complex equivalence P with inverse R, set g=η_I followed by R(f) and D_n=R^n I with transition R^n(g). Let Y=colim D. The maps R^n(g) followed by R(j_n) define a cocone to RY. Its induced map σ:Y→RY is invertible: the maps j_(n+1):R(D_n)→Y induce its inverse because R preserves colimits. On j_n, the first composite is R^n(g) followed by j_(n+1), hence j_n; on R(j_n), the other composite is R(R^n(g)) followed by R(j_(n+1)), hence R(j_n). Colimit uniqueness gives both inverse equations.

proof.text: Put τ=P(σ) followed by ε_Y:PY≅Y. The equation j_0 σ=g R(j_0), counit naturality, and the triangle identity give P(j_0) τ=f j_0. This constructs an invertible chain action directly. Its components and the differentials of Y define a complex B of fixed pairs, because τ is a chain map. The square-zero and shape identities are checked by faithful forgetting.

proof.text: Take $M=Q_{\mathcal B}\widetilde C$. Exactness of $U$ and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identify $D(U)M$ with $QC$, and the induced structure $\theta_M$ with $Q(\tau)$. Put $e=aQ(j_0)^{-1}:QC\xrightarrow{\sim}N$. The actual chain equality $\tau P(j_0)=j_0f$ becomes $Q(\tau)D(P)(Q(j_0))=Q(j_0)Q(f)$. Multiplying on the left by $e$ gives $eQ(\tau)D(P)(Q(j_0))=aQ(f)=vD(P)(a)$. Cancel the invertible $D(P)(Q(j_0))$ on the right to obtain $e\theta_M=vD(P)(e)$, with the termwise-to-derived identifications just specified.

proof.text: Exactness and faithfulness of the source-library forgetful functor U give UH^q(M)≅H^q(D(U)M)≅H^q(N), using mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso. A faithful exact functor reflects zero homology, so every interval of vanishing for N is one for M. Any isomorphism-invariant object property transports along the same composite cohomology isomorphism. Neither boundedness nor closure of the property under colimits is needed for these conclusions.
